clue.text: Meeting with prisoner is a sensational success

parts.note: POW is the standard abbreviation for prisoner of war
a wow is a smash hit, something that knocks people out

explanation.surface: An encounter that includes a convict turns out to be a triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: A powwow is a conference or discussion, originally a gathering of Native American peoples.

clue.text: Kind of crossing made by Drake's ship

definitions.meaning: a ... crossing is a British pedestrian crossing with lights the walker controls
Sir Francis Drake's Golden Hind sailed from England under its first name

explanation.surface: A type of road crossing apparently built by an Elizabethan sea captain's vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made by' is a link. A pelican crossing is a British street crossing; Drake renamed his ship the Golden Hind during his voyage round the world.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are names: a type of British road crossing and the original name of Drake's flagship.

clue.text: Financial gains from the branches

definitions.meaning: unexpected sums of money that fall into one's lap
fruit blown down off a tree by the wind

explanation.surface: Money made from a company's local offices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'branches' suggests a bank or shop network, but the second sense is orchard fruit knocked off the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Unexpected money is a windfall, and so is fruit the wind brings down from a tree.

clue.text: Vegetables that need to be set in soon

indicators.note: to set is to arrange or fix in a new way, so the letters of the words that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener's note about vegetables that must be planted shortly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' is the anagram signal on IN and SOON; gardeners also plant small bulbs called onion sets, which makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Onions are a bulb vegetable used throughout cooking.

clue.text: Bottom gear

parts.note: reads like the lowest gear of a car, but means clothing worn on one's bottom

explanation.definitionFit: Underpants for women are clothing worn over the backside, hence garments for the bottom.

clue.text: Where cricketers practise catches

definitions.meaning: batsmen practise in enclosures of netting behind the pavilion
to net something is to catch it, as in a net

explanation.surface: Cricket practice is where players work on taking catches.
explanation.definitionFit: Netted practice areas are where cricketers train, and to net is to capture or take.

clue.text: Fifty in carol involving bells

indicators.note: to involve is to wrap up and entangle, so the letters are tangled into a new order

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Fifty singers take part in a carol accompanied by bells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' looks like a container signal, putting fifty in a carol, but here it means tangling: the anagram signal over the whole pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A carillon is a set of tuned bells played from a keyboard, usually in a tower.

clue.text: He's forced to live off his land

definitions.text: He's forced to live off his land

parts.words: He's forced to live off his land
parts.note: 'live off the land' suggests foraging, but here 'off' means away from his homeland

explanation.definitionFit: A banished person must make a home outside the country of their birth.

clue.text: Recommend advocate

definitions.meaning: to put forward an idea for consideration
here a verb: to propose or argue for something

explanation.surface: Put in a good word for a lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'advocate' reads as a lawyer, but here it is a verb meaning propose.
explanation.definitionFit: To propose a plan is both to recommend it and to advocate it.

clue.text: Pulse is fast at one fifty

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting before Easter
I is the Roman numeral one
L is the Roman numeral fifty

explanation.surface: A heartbeat stays steady at a rate of one hundred and fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' and 'fast' suggest a heart rate; pulses are also edible seeds such as beans and peas.
explanation.definitionFit: A lentil is a pulse, one of the dried edible seeds of a legume.

clue.text: British capital

definitions.meaning: relating to the pound, the British currency
an old-fashioned word for excellent, first-rate

explanation.surface: London, or the money of the United Kingdom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'British capital' reads as London or UK money; split it into British (as in the pound) and capital in the sense excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: The pound is the British currency of that name, and the adjective also means excellent or thoroughly worthy.

clue.text: Painter, sanctimonious and a fool in company

parts.note: pi is a slang shortening of pious, meaning sanctimonious

indicators.note: the fool is placed inside the abbreviation for company

parts.note: an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: An artist described as self-righteous and foolish among his companions.
explanation.definitionFit: Pablo Picasso was the Spanish painter who co-founded Cubism.

clue.text: In France, a hot drink of a nicer blend

indicators.note: a blend is a mixture, so the letters of the words before it are mixed together

explanation.surface: A coffee in France made from a finer blend of beans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blend' sounds like coffee talk but it is the anagram signal on OF A NICER.
explanation.definitionFit: Black coffee is called this in French, and it is drunk hot.

clue.text: Maintain there's some body in the beer

indicators.note: the body part is placed inside the word for beer

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
a leg is a part of the body

explanation.surface: Someone insists a body has been found in the beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some body' reads as somebody, a person; here it means a part of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: To allege is to claim or assert that something is so, often without proof.

clue.text: Edward lifts firm with spirit and dignity

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting the name abbreviation turns it upward, so it reads backwards

parts.note: Ed is a short form of Edward
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: Edward boosts a company with liquor and a sense of self-respect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifts' sounds like help, but in a down clue it turns ED upward to give DE.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorum is proper behaviour and dignified propriety.

clue.text: Wriggly line on the map of Africa

indicators.note: wriggly means twisting and squirming, so the letters of the word are twisted round

explanation.surface: A winding line drawn on a map of Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wriggly' is the anagram signal on LINE, and also pictures a winding river on the map.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nile is the great river of north-east Africa, drawn on any map of the continent.

clue.text: Robust shoes will be

parts.note: shoes are shaped on a cobbler's last, so durable shoes are built on one

explanation.definitionFit: Durable things are built to endure, and shoes are moulded on a shoemaker's form called a last.

clue.text: One doesn't like to show it

definitions.text: One doesn't like to show it

parts.words: One doesn't like to show it
parts.note: reads as reluctance to reveal something, but means what someone who dislikes another displays

explanation.definitionFit: Hostility or strong dislike is what a person who does not like someone shows.

clue.text: In the main, it's classed as vermin

definitions.text: In the main, it's classed as vermin

parts.words: In the main, it's classed as vermin
parts.note: 'in the main' seems to mean generally, but the main is a drain pipe where this rodent lives

explanation.definitionFit: A brown rodent living in drains, considered a pest.

clue.text: Devilish control

parts.note: control of a person by a demon or the Devil

explanation.definitionFit: A demon is said to take over someone in a state of being possessed.

clue.text: Not much of an opening for this sort of camera

definitions.text: Not much of an opening for this sort of camera

parts.words: Not much of an opening for this sort of camera
parts.note: reads as a poor career opportunity, but describes a tiny aperture used instead of a lens

explanation.definitionFit: A simple lensless camera takes its image through a tiny hole made with a pin.

clue.text: Choose to break new ground

definitions.meaning: a pointed tool used to break up hard earth

explanation.surface: Decide to start something innovative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break new ground' sounds like innovating; literally a pick breaks the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To select is to pick, and a pickaxe breaks up earth.

clue.text: Sauce boat now costing more

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat
prices that are up have risen

explanation.surface: A gravy boat that has become more expensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sauce boat' suggests a gravy jug; 'Sauce' is the definition and 'boat' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Ketchup is a tomato sauce used as a condiment.

clue.text: A quarter-cent rise

parts.note: S, south, is one of the four quarters or compass points

explanation.surface: A tiny price increase of a quarter of a cent.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords a 'quarter' is a compass point, here S.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascent is a climb or upward movement.

clue.text: Having a down on

parts.note: 'having a down on' suggests disliking someone, but means bearing a soft pile on cloth

explanation.definitionFit: Fabric with a raised soft pile on its surface is described this way.

clue.text: Minister of the armed forces

parts.note: reads as a government post but means a clergyman serving soldiers

explanation.definitionFit: A military chaplain is a minister of religion attached to the services.

clue.text: Have insufficient funds and don't finish the course

definitions.meaning: a runner who stops before the finish has not covered the full distance

explanation.surface: Being out of cash and failing to complete a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link between the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: To lack enough money is to be short of it, and a race stopped early falls short of the distance.

clue.text: Holy Roman Emperor to turn to

indicators.note: turning the first small word round reads it backwards

explanation.surface: Someone appeals to a medieval monarch for help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' reverses the first TO to give OT, followed by the second TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto the Great was the first Holy Roman Emperor, and several later emperors bore the name.

clue.text: A doubter disposed to be stubborn

indicators.note: disposed can mean arranged or set out, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sceptic inclined to be obstinate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposed to be' reads as inclined; 'disposed' alone is the anagram signal on A DOUBTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Obdurate means hard-hearted and unwilling to change one's mind.

clue.text: Enjoy the pickles

definitions.meaning: a piquant condiment such as chutney or pickle; the plural suits the mass sense

explanation.surface: Someone takes pleasure in pickled vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: To savour is to relish, and a tangy chutney-like condiment goes by the same name.

clue.text: Pilot's emergency exit

parts.note: an airman leaving a stricken aircraft by being fired out in his seat

explanation.definitionFit: Throwing out a pilot by ejector seat is a forcible expulsion from the cockpit.

clue.text: Put off one's retirement

parts.note: sounds like delaying leaving work, but means delaying going to bed

explanation.definitionFit: Not going to bed until late is delaying the night's retiring.
